item.text:
**Assessment**: Mostly yes. The 2024 record points to broad, cross-group distribution of gains: investment plus tax relief, social housing, municipal support, East-West cohesion, women’s advancement, and migrant inclusion. I did not find direct evidence of patronage toward regime supporters or oligarchic redistribution. The main negatives are late-2024 instability and some hardline rhetoric, not a clear favoritism pattern.

That supports a rules-based, broadly shared growth strategy rather than insider privilege. | 5B.8, 5B.6, 5B.7 |

That is broad distribution across households and regions, not a regime-supporter windfall. | 5B.8, 5B.6 |

That points to support for weaker localities rather than concentrating gains in favored centers. | 5B.8, 5B.6 |

That is direct regional-fairness evidence. | 5B.8, 5B.6 |

That is not blanket scapegoating of a group. | 5B.8, 5B.7 |
| Counter | German coalition collapses | Reuters via Investing.com | 2024-11-06 | https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/explainergerman-coalition-collapses-what-comes-next-3706936 | The coalition collapse created political chaos and weakened continuity, which undercut stable redistribution and predictable delivery late in 2024. This is a practical negative, not proof of favoritism. | 5B.8, 5B.7 |
| Counter | Bundestag confidence vote | Deutscher Bundestag | 2024-12-16 | https://www.bundestag.de/dokumente/textarchiv/2024/kw47-vertrauensfrage-1030198 | The large confidence loss confirmed year-end instability and reduced policy continuity. Again, this weakens broad fairness in practice, but it does not show patronage or supporter-only allocation. | 5B.8, 5B.7 |

Search gap: I found strong evidence for broad-based, cross-group distributional intent, but no direct source-backed example of Scholz privileging regime supporters, cronies, or oligarchs in 2024. I also did not find a direct quantitative distributional study in the retrieved sources, so the judgment rests on policy statements and public actions rather than measured distributional outcomes.
